title: 爱丽丝掉进的洞
author: Lewis Carroll（WordVerse 改写版）
one_line: 一瓶药水、一池眼泪，和一场人人都得奖的赛跑。

sentences.en: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the river bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures and no formal conversations in it, and she wondered, with a yawn, what in the world was the use of a book that neither showed pictures nor talked sense.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝坐在河岸上，靠着姐姐，开始觉得无聊透顶：她偷看过一两回姐姐读的那本书，里面既没有插图，也没有像样的对话；她打着哈欠想，一本既不画给人看、又不跟人说正经话的书，到底有什么用处。

sentences.en: The sun was hot, the shade under the hedge was thin, and a soft weight of sleepiness pressed upon her eyelids; her sister was reading a book without pictures or conversations, about statistics or history — something equally patient — and Alice, who liked her lessons short and her stories illustrated, decided the afternoon was a great deal too long for either.
sentences.zh: 太阳很晒，树篱下的荫凉又很薄，一阵困意像温水一样压上她的眼皮；姐姐读的那本书没有插图、没有对话，讲的是统计学或历史——反正一样需要耐心——而爱丽丝这个人，功课喜欢短的，故事喜欢带画的，于是断定这个下午对哪一样来说都实在太长了。

sentences.en: Suddenly a white rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her, saying to itself, "Oh dear, I shall be too late," and Alice thought nothing of this, for a talking rabbit is only one degree stranger than a hurried one; but when the rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket, looked at it, frowned, and hurried on, Alice rose to her feet, burning with curiosity.
sentences.zh: 忽然，一只粉眼睛的白兔子从她身边跑过，嘴里念着"哎呀，我要迟到了"；爱丽丝并没觉得这有什么奇怪——会说话的兔子，不过是比匆匆忙忙的兔子再怪上一分罢了；可当那兔子从背心口袋里掏出一块规规矩矩的怀表，看了一眼，皱了皱眉，又匆匆赶路时，爱丽丝站了起来，好奇心烧得她坐不住。

sentences.en: She ran across the field after it, just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge, and in another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering, in the hurry of the moment, how in the world she was to get out again — which is the sort of thought that arrives only after its owner is already falling.
sentences.zh: 她跑过田野去追，正赶上看见它钻进树篱下一个大大的兔子洞；转眼之间，爱丽丝也跟着跳了进去——在那阵慌忙里，她压根没想过，出去了该怎么再出来；这一类念头，向来只在主人已经落下去之后，才姗姗来迟。

sentences.en: The hole went down like a deep vertical well, yet she fell not quickly but gently, slowly enough to look about her and to take an inventory of the walls, which were lined with cupboards and bookshelves in tidy formation, and with jars of jam hanging on pegs beside maps and pictures, all in the most finished order, as if somebody were expected.
sentences.zh: 那洞像一口深井一样笔直向下，可她下坠得并不快，慢得足够她边落边打量四周：洞壁上排着碗柜和书架，整整齐齐，煞有队形，挂钉上还吊着一罐罐果酱，旁边是地图和画片——一切都收拾得妥妥帖帖，仿佛随时有客人要来。

sentences.en: She took down a jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE, was disappointed to find it empty, and, fearing to drop it upon anybody below, she managed to put it into one of the cupboards as she passed — which was, she thought afterwards, very proper conduct for a falling girl.
sentences.zh: 她取下一只标着"橘子酱"的罐子，却失望地发现里面是空的；她怕随手一扔砸到下面的人，落过碗柜时便设法把它放了进去——她后来想，对一个边下落边办正事的小姑娘来说，这算是很有分寸的举止了。

sentences.en: Down, down she went, trying to predict how far she had fallen, and guessing it must be near the centre of the earth, half believing that the whole universe had turned upside down with her, and that she would never arrive anywhere at all.
sentences.zh: 她落啊落，落啊落，一面猜自己已经落到多深——准是快到地心了吧——一面又半信半疑，觉得整个宇宙都跟着她翻了个个儿，而她永远到不了任何地方。

sentences.en: "After a fall like this," she said aloud to nobody, "I shall think nothing of tumbling down the stairs at home; I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it; why, I might fall right through the earth and come out among the antipodes, and fancy asking a native the way back."
sentences.zh: "经过这样一摔，"她对着空处大声说，"在家从楼梯上滚下来根本不算什么；现在就算我想晕，也晕不起来了；没准我能一直穿过地球，从地球背面那头掉出去——你想想，还得开口找当地人问回程的路。"

sentences.en: She tried to remember her multiplication tables as she fell, which gave the darkness the pleasing form of a lesson, and she found she could still say them, if a little slurred, which suggested to her that falling, on the whole, agreed with her memory — and this comforted her, as multiplication has comforted falling girls from time immemorial.
sentences.zh: 下落时她试着背乘法口诀，这就给黑暗安上了一种功课的好形式；她发现自己居然还背得出——尽管有点含混——由此她认定，下落这件事，总体来说，不碍她的记性；这个发现让她安心，须知自古以来，乘法口诀安慰过多少往下掉的小姑娘。

sentences.en: Presently the shelves ran out, and she dropped past the last of them into an amorphous darkness that had no top, no bottom, and no shape her eyes could honestly name; the fall, which had seemed gentle, now felt long enough to be a residence.
sentences.zh: 不久搁板到头了；她落过最后一块，坠进一团无定形的黑暗里——没有顶，没有底，也没有眼睛叫得出名字的形状；这场原本温柔的下落，如今长得都快够资格称为定居了。

sentences.en: The darkness did not frighten her so much as it informed her — for it was perfectly quiet, perfectly empty, and perfectly unlike anything in her lessons — that the world she knew had been quietly folded up and put away, and that some other version of it had been unfolded in its place.
sentences.zh: 这黑暗与其说吓着她，不如说是通知了她：它安安静静、空空荡荡，和她功课里的任何东西都不像——她所熟悉的那个世界，已经被悄悄叠好收起来了，另一个版本，正在原地被展开。

sentences.en: At last the fall ended all at once: a thump, a heap of dry sticks and leaves, and Alice found herself sitting on a bank, unhurt, in another world, looking about her with wide eyes and not one bone out of order.
sentences.zh: 下坠终于戛然而止：噗的一声，一堆干树枝和树叶；爱丽丝发现自己坐在一层落叶上，毫发无伤地置身另一个世界，睁大眼睛四下张望，一根骨头也没错位。

sentences.en: Before her ran a passage a little larger than a rat-hole, and along it came the white rabbit, trotting back and talking to itself still; "Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!" said the rabbit, and it popped down its own hole and vanished.
sentences.zh: 面前是一条比耗子洞大不了多少的走廊，那只白兔子正沿着它往回小跑，嘴里还在自言自语；"我的耳朵和胡须啊，越来越晚了！"兔子说完，一头钻进自己的洞，不见了。

sentences.en: Alice followed it at once, at a run, burning with the same curiosity, and the little passage turned a corner, and the light at the end of it opened into a long, low hall, lit by a row of lamps hanging from the roof.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝立刻拔腿追了上去，还是那股烧人的好奇心；走廊拐了个弯，尽头那点亮光豁然敞开，变成一间又长又矮的大厅，屋顶下挂着一排灯，把厅里照得亮堂堂。

questions.q: Why did Alice doubt the use of her sister's book?
options: It was far too long for one afternoon.
It had no pictures and no formal conversations in it.
It was written in a foreign language.
It belonged to a grown-up library.
questions.explain: 第1句 "it had no pictures and no formal conversations in it, and she wondered... what in the world was the use of a book that neither showed pictures nor talked sense"。

questions.q: What finally made Alice stand up and chase the rabbit?
options: The rabbit spoke aloud to itself.
The rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket.
The rabbit had remarkable pink eyes.
The rabbit wore a smart waistcoat.
questions.explain: 第3句写她起初不以为然，"but when the rabbit drew a formal watch from its waistcoat pocket, looked at it, frowned, and hurried on, Alice rose to her feet, burning with curiosity"——掏出怀表才是转折点。

questions.q: What did Alice find inside the jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE?
options: Sweet orange marmalade.
A little golden key.
A paper label saying DRINK ME.
Nothing — the jar was empty.
questions.explain: 第6句 "She took down a jar marked ORANGE MARMALADE, was disappointed to find it empty"，罐子是空的，她还很有分寸地把它放回了碗柜。

questions.q: The quiet darkness is said to "inform" Alice of something. What has happened, in her own understanding?
options: She is about to land on the moon.
The world she knew has been folded away, and another version of it unfolded in its place.
She has been asleep on the river bank all along.
She has fallen all the way through the earth.
questions.explain: 第11句 "the world she knew had been quietly folded up and put away, and that some other version of it had been unfolded in its place"——由此可推知，她已认定自己换到另一个世界的版本里了。

questions.q: With vert meaning to turn, what is "vertigo" in "I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it"?
options: A great thirst.
A fear of rabbits.
The dizzy, head-turning feeling of falling from a height.
A pain in the feet after running.
questions.explain: 第8句 "I shall think nothing of tumbling down the stairs at home; I could not feel vertigo now if I wished for it"——vertigo（词根 vert，转）指从高处跌落时那种天旋地转的眩晕感。

sentences.en: At the end of the long low hall stood a tiny door, only about fifteen inches high, and through the keyhole Alice saw the loveliest garden she had ever dreamed of — bright flowers, cool fountains, and beds of flowers she could not name — and she longed to get into it with all her heart, and, being ten times too large, she could not.
sentences.zh: 又长又矮的大厅尽头有一扇小门，只有大约十五英寸高；透过锁孔，爱丽丝看见了她梦寐以求的最美的花园——鲜艳的花、清凉的喷泉，还有许多叫不上名字的花圃；她一心想进去，可她比门大了十倍，进不去。

sentences.en: She sat down and wept, then scolded herself for weeping, quite like a nurse scolding a child, and quoted her own lessons back at herself like a disagreeable governess: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a great girl like you, crying in this way — stop this minute, I tell you!"
sentences.zh: 她坐下来哭了一场，接着又为哭鼻子训斥自己，活像保姆训孩子，还像个讨厌的家庭教师，把自己的功课背给自己听："真不害臊，这么大个姑娘了，这样哭鼻子——立刻给我停下，听见没有！"

sentences.en: Presently her eye fell upon a very small bottle standing on the glass table, tied to it with a paper label bearing, in neat formal letters, the words DRINK ME; and she found a little golden key on the same table, which she guessed, correctly, belonged to the little door.
sentences.zh: 不久，她看见玻璃桌上立着一只很小的瓶子，系着纸标签，用端正的正式字体写着"喝我"两个字；同一张桌上还躺着一把小金钥匙，她猜——猜得没错——正是那扇小门的。

sentences.en: Her lessons had informed her that if you drink much from a bottle marked poison, it will almost certainly contradict you sooner or later — that is, disagree with you, "disagree" being the polite word for it — so she checked the label carefully for that dangerous word, and was glad to find it absent.
sentences.zh: 功课教过她：标着"毒药"的瓶子，喝下去早晚会"反驳"你——也就是跟你过不去，"过不去"是客气些的说法——于是她把标签仔仔细细检查了一遍，看有没有那个危险的字眼，很高兴没有找到。

sentences.en: "It seems to have no poison in it, and it is only polite to drink what one is formally invited to drink," she reasoned; the strange formula inside tasted of cherry tart, custard, pine-apple, roast turkey and hot buttered toast, all in a single sip, and she finished it to the last drop, for a child at her stage of life is a scientist.
sentences.zh: "看来里面没有毒，况且人家正式请我喝，喝了才礼貌，"她这样推理；瓶里那古怪的配方，一口下去，樱桃馅饼、蛋奶糊、菠萝、烤火鸡和热黄油吐司全都在了；她把它喝到了最后一滴——她这个年纪的孩子，个个都是科学家。

sentences.en: A warm transformation swept through her, and in a moment she was barely ten inches high; she was delighted at first, for now she could creep under the door — but she had forgotten the little golden key, and her new size had dictated a fresh problem instead of a solution, for the key lay on the table, far above her head.
sentences.zh: 一阵暖烘烘的变化涌遍全身，转眼间她只有十英寸高了；起先她高兴坏了——这下能从门底下爬进去了——可她忘了那把小金钥匙；新身材没有解决旧难题，反倒指定了一道新的：钥匙还躺在桌上，远远高过她的头顶。

sentences.en: Nothing remained but to try her old verses, and to see whether her head had shrunk along with her body; she began to recite, but the words came out all wrong, her diction stumbling over lines she had once known perfectly, and she concluded that she must have been transformed into some other little girl, who did not know her lessons properly.
sentences.zh: 她只剩一个法子：背背旧诗，看看脑袋是不是跟着身子一起缩小了；她开口一背，词全跑偏了，措辞在从前烂熟的诗行上一跤接一跤地绊倒；于是她断定，自己准是变成了另一个小姑娘，一个功课学得不怎么样的。

sentences.en: "I am sure I am not Ada, and I am sure I cannot be Mabel, for she knows such a very little; I must have been changed for one of them" — and as she said it a tear rolled down one cheek, and then a whole procession of tears, and nothing in the world could be done to stop them.
sentences.zh: "我肯定不是艾达，也肯定当不了梅布尔，她懂得那么少；我一定是被换成了她们中的一个"——话音未落，一颗泪珠从一边脸颊滚下来，随后是整整一队眼泪，天底下没有任何办法能拦住它们。

sentences.en: Soon she found a little glass box lying under the table, and inside it a very small cake, on which currants had spelled, in letters even more formal than the label's, the words EAT ME; she put the box in her lap and set herself to think, as well as a girl in her position could.
sentences.zh: 很快她在桌子底下找到一只小玻璃盒，里面有一块很小的蛋糕，上面的葡萄干拼出"吃我"两个字，那字体比标签上的还要正式；她把盒子搁在膝上，让自己尽力思考——一个处在这种境地的小姑娘，能想到多远就想多远。

sentences.en: "If this makes me larger, I can reach the key; if it makes me smaller, I can creep under the door; either way I shall get into the garden, and it is only the size of the middle that puzzles me" — which is the kind of reasoning that looks admirable until it is tested, and hers was about to be.
sentences.zh: "要是吃了变大，我够得着钥匙；要是变小，我能从门底下爬过去——不管哪样都能进花园；麻烦只出在中间那个不大不小的尺寸上。"——这一类推理，在没受检验之前总显得头头是道，而她这套，马上就要受检验了。

sentences.en: She ate a piece, and the metamorphosis was not gentle: she grew, and grew, and grew, until her head pressed against the ceiling — nine feet high at the least — and one arm went out the window, and one foot up the chimney, whichever came handiest.
sentences.zh: 她吃了一块，这次的变形毫不温柔：她长啊，长啊，长个不停，直到头顶顶住天花板——至少也有九英尺高——一条胳膊伸出了窗外，一只脚翘上了烟囱，哪儿顺手往哪儿去。

sentences.en: Looking down at her own vast shoes, she felt that something deformed and monstrous had replaced the little girl she had been, and she began to cry again; and the tears were enormous, being the tears of a giantess, and the hall began to be a wet place.
sentences.zh: 低头看着自己巨大的鞋，她觉得有什么畸形而吓人的庞然大物，顶替了原来那个小姑娘；她又哭了起来——这回的眼泪也是巨人的眼泪，一颗颗大得吓人，大厅渐渐成了个湿乎乎的地方。

sentences.en: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself," she told the giant, meaning herself, "crying over nothing in a great hall like this; you should have a bonnet to drop your tears into, or a proper handkerchief, either of which would be formal and useful" — and the great tears rolled down all the same.
sentences.zh: "真不害臊，"她对那巨人训道——也就是训她自己——"守着这么大的厅堂，没事就哭鼻子；你该有顶帽子接眼泪，或者有块正正经经的手帕，哪一样都体面又管用"——可那些大大的泪珠，还是照样一颗颗滚下来。

sentences.en: She sat, enormous and weeping, in the middle of the hall, and wondered whether she would ever be the right size again, or whether she was now a version of herself that would never fit through any door in the world.
sentences.zh: 她坐在大厅正中，巨大，淌着泪，心里嘀咕：自己还能不能变回合适的尺寸，还是从此成了又一个版本的自己——一个再也钻不进世上任何一扇门的版本。

questions.q: Why did Alice decide the bottle was probably safe to drink?
options: The label was written in formal letters.
She had checked it carefully and found no mark of poison on it.
It smelled like hot buttered toast.
The glass table looked clean and honest.
questions.explain: 第4句她想起毒药瓶的教训，"she checked the label carefully for that dangerous word, and was glad to find it absent"——查过标签，没有"毒药"字样，她才敢喝。

questions.q: When a poison bottle is said to "contradict" you, what is meant?
options: The bottle will start an argument with you.
The poison will disagree with you — make you seriously ill.
The label will contradict the taste.
You will forget all your lessons.
questions.explain: 第4句她自己给出了注解——"that is, disagree with you, 'disagree' being the polite word for it"——contradict（contra 反 + dict 说）在这里是双关：字面像"出言反驳"，实指毒药跟你"过不去"，让你中毒。

questions.q: After shrinking to ten inches, what new problem did Alice face?
options: She could no longer see the little door.
The golden key lay on the table, far above her head.
The door had grown even smaller.
She had lost her old verses entirely.
questions.explain: 第6句 "her new size had dictated a fresh problem instead of a solution, for the key lay on the table, far above her head"——人变小了，钥匙却够不着了。

questions.q: After eating the cake, why does Alice feel "something deformed and monstrous" has replaced the little girl she was?
options: Her body has become ugly and too large for the room, and she no longer recognizes herself in it.
A real monster has taken her place in the mirror.
Her shoes have been stolen by the rabbit.
She has grown so small that she cannot see herself.
questions.explain: 第12句她低头看着自己的巨鞋、头抵天花板、臂出窗外——身体大得装不下这个房间，与第11句的 metamorphosis 对照可知：她觉得这具失控变形的身体顶替了原来的小姑娘，自我都要认不出了。

questions.q: With morph meaning form, shape, what does "metamorphosis" describe in sentence 11?
options: A polite conversation about weather.
A change from one form into another — here, Alice's sudden enormous growth.
A very slow walk across a hall.
A kind of cake baked with currants.
questions.explain: 第11句 "She ate a piece, and the metamorphosis was not gentle: she grew, and grew, and grew"——metamorphosis（meta 变 + morph 形）指形态的根本改变，即她吃下蛋糕后身体的急剧变形。

sentences.en: Alice was still enormous, and her tears were enormous too, and before long the long low hall held a pool of salt water four inches deep and half a mile wide, if you counted it the way she counted it, which was emotionally rather than mathematically, though her arithmetic masters would have called it four inches and no more.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝哭的时候还是那么巨大，泪水也跟着巨大；不一会儿，又长又矮的大厅里就积起了一池咸水，四英寸深，足有半英里宽——如果是照她的算法算的话：她的算法从来是感情用事，不是数学用事；虽然她的算术老师们，只会管它叫四英寸，一寸不多。

sentences.en: "I wish I had not cried so much," she said, swimming about the hall in a rising despair; but it was already too late to avert a flood of her own making, and the flood, in the manner of floods, did not care whose it was; the water stood, in fact, at her chin, and rising.
sentences.zh: "早知道就不哭那么久了，"她在厅里划着水说，越划越绝望；可要躲开这场自己亲手哭出来的洪水，已经太迟了；而洪水向来是洪水的做派：它是谁的，根本不在乎——那水，事实上已经齐到她的下巴，还在涨。

sentences.en: Presently she heard a splash in the middle of the pool, and a mouse swam towards her; and in this strange version of the world it seemed to Alice quite natural that the mouse should talk, though what it would say was anybody's guess.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，池子中央传来扑通一声，一只老鼠朝她游了过来；在这个奇怪版本的世界里，老鼠会说话，爱丽丝觉得再自然不过——只是它要说什么，谁也猜不着。

sentences.en: "O Mouse," she began, borrowing the diction of her brother's Latin grammar, "do you know the way out of this pool? I am very tired of swimming about here, O Mouse" — for she had read that this was the correct form of address, and had never once been contradicted on the point by anybody who mattered.
sentences.zh: "老鼠啊，"她开口了，措辞 borrowed 自哥哥的拉丁语法书，"你知道怎么游出这个池子吗？在这儿划来划去我实在累了，老鼠啊。"——因为她读到过，这才是标准的称呼格式，而这一点，从来没有哪个要紧的人反驳过她。

sentences.en: The Mouse said nothing, but looked at her uneasily, and only later, in cool retrospect, did Alice understand how rude that opening must have sounded; and the Mouse, whose history was indeed long and sad, gave her one more chance before going away — which was, of mice, a very generous decision.
sentences.zh: 老鼠没作声，只是不安地看了她一眼；很久之后冷静回想，爱丽丝才明白那个开场白听上去有多失礼；而这只老鼠——它的经历确实又长又惨——决定再给她一次机会，之后再走不迟；以老鼠的规矩，这算得上宽宏大量了。

sentences.en: "Mine is a long and a sad tale," said the Mouse with a sigh, "and it is the driest thing I know, which is exactly what you want, being so wet."
sentences.zh: "我的故事（tale）又长又惨，"老鼠叹了口气说，"也是我知道的最干巴巴的东西——你们湿成这样，正需要它。"

sentences.en: "A sad tail?" said Alice, looking at the Mouse's tail with great wonder; "it is certainly a long one, but I should call it wet rather than sad, and curly rather than either" — and the Mouse, whose patience was already a thin coat in the rain, explained rather coldly that it had meant its history, not its tail.
sentences.zh: "惨的尾巴（tail）？"爱丽丝好奇地盯着老鼠的尾巴说，"它确实挺长，可我觉得它湿乎乎的，不算惨——要说卷，倒还沾点边。"——老鼠的耐心本就薄得像雨里的一层外套，它冷冷地解释：自己说的是经历，不是尾巴。

sentences.en: Alice hurried to divert the conversation to safer ground, and the safest ground she could find in her whole stock of knowledge was her cat Dinah, a wonderful mouse-catching creature; and at the name of Dinah the whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water itself had heard of cats, and Dinah had never in her life been so influential.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝赶紧把话题引到更安全的地方去，而她全部学问里最保险的话题，就是她的猫黛娜——一只抓老鼠的好手；"黛娜"两个字一出口，整池水仿佛都僵住了，好像连水都听说过猫的厉害；黛娜这辈子，还从没这么有过影响力。

sentences.en: "Let us get to the shore," said the Mouse, rising in the water with a shiver that converted its fur into a wet flag, "and there I will tell you my story, and you will understand things" — and Alice, apologizing in every direction at once, swam after it as fast as she could.
sentences.zh: "咱们上岸吧，"老鼠从水里立起身，抖得皮毛成了一面湿旗，"到岸上我把故事讲给你听，你就明白一些事了"——爱丽丝朝着四面八方同时道歉，拼尽全力跟在它后面游。

sentences.en: When she stood up in the pool, Alice saw her own doing clearly for the first time: she had converted a private sorrow into a public sea, and the hall had undergone a complete transformation, from a place where she had sat alone into a place where everybody else was obliged to swim.
sentences.zh: 站在池子里，爱丽丝头一回看清了自己的所作所为：她把一场私人的伤心，转换成了一片公共的海；这间大厅也经历了彻底的变形——从她一个人坐着的地方，变成了所有人都不得不游泳的地方。

sentences.en: On the bank stood a crowd of unhappy creatures, dripping — a duck, a dodo, an eaglet, a lory, and several others whose names Alice did not catch — and they were uniform only in being wet through, and uniform, which is a kind of politeness among strangers, in saying nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 岸上站着一大群湿淋淋的可怜动物——鸭子、渡渡鸟、小鹰、小鹦鹉，还有些名字爱丽丝没听清的——它们唯一一致的地方，就是个个浑身湿透；它们对这一点也一律只字不提——在陌生动物中间，这算是一种礼貌。

sentences.en: They looked at one another and shivered, and the dodo, who seemed to be the wisest and was, at least, the roundest, remarked at last that the best thing to get them dry would be a Caucus-race, and the Mouse, in the formal way of mice, suggested first its history, the dodo's idea being the only one put forward with the advantage of motion.
sentences.zh: 它们面面相觑，抖个不停；看起来最智慧、至少最圆的渡渡鸟最后发话：要把大家弄干，最好的办法是来一场会议式赛跑；老鼠则按老鼠们一本正经的规矩，先提议讲讲自己的经历——结果被全体谢绝了；渡渡鸟的主意，是全场唯一自带运动量的一条。

sentences.en: Alice promised, in her politest manner, to listen to the Mouse's history once they were dry, though privately she was more interested in the strange animals, who stood about like a wet audience that has not been told whether it is a congregation or a jury, and she could not settle which either.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝以她最礼貌的方式许诺：等大家干了，一定专心听老鼠的经历；尽管私底下，她更感兴趣的是这群奇怪的动物——它们站在那儿，像一群没弄清自己是来听道的还是来当陪审的湿淋淋的听众；而这两样究竟哪一样，她也定不下来。

sentences.en: And so they stood on the bank, wet and solemn, the tears of one little girl, grown enormous and then shed, now lapping at all their feet — a fact which nobody chose to mention, because the girl who had done the crying was the only one offering to organize the drying, and had already begun, in her head, to do it.
sentences.zh: 于是它们站在岸上，湿着，庄重着；一个小姑娘的眼泪——先长得巨大、再一涌而出——此刻正轻轻拍打着所有人的脚背；这件事谁也不肯提，因为那个哭出这场水的姑娘，偏偏是唯一一个站出来张罗烘干的——而且她已经在心里张罗起来了。

questions.q: What caused the pool that Alice swam in?
options: The white rabbit's spilled tea.
The tears of the giant Alice herself.
Rain falling through the ceiling.
The river rising into the hole.
questions.explain: 第1句写她还巨大时"her tears were enormous too"，四英寸深的水很快积满大厅，第2句更点明"too late to avert a flood of her own making"——是她自己哭出来的洪水。

questions.q: What mistake does Alice make about the Mouse's "sad tale"?
options: She thinks the Mouse is lying about it.
She hears "tail" and looks at the Mouse's tail instead.
She believes the tale is far too short.
She thinks it belongs to the dodo.
questions.explain: 第6句老鼠说的是 tale（故事），第7句爱丽丝却去端详它的 tail（尾巴）说"it is certainly a long one, but I should call it wet rather than sad"——tale 与 tail 同音，她听岔了。

questions.q: What happened when Alice mentioned the name Dinah?
options: The animals cheered for the cat.
The whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water had heard of cats.
The dodo proposed the race at once.
The Mouse swam away without a word.
questions.explain: 第8句 "at the name of Dinah the whole pool seemed to stiffen, as if the water itself had heard of cats"——在老鼠面前夸猫，全场都僵住了。

questions.q: Standing up in the pool, Alice "saw her own doing clearly for the first time". What did she realize?
options: That her private sorrow had become a public sea that others were forced to swim in.
That the pool was secretly fed by the river.
That the animals had brought the water in buckets.
That she was still growing larger.
questions.explain: 第10句 "she had converted a private sorrow into a public sea"——她把一己的伤心变成了所有人的麻烦，由第14句"眼泪正拍打所有动物的脚背"可印证。

questions.q: With vert meaning to turn, what does "avert" mean in "too late to avert a flood"?
options: To turn aside or prevent something from happening.
To swim quickly through deep water.
To cry louder than before.
To measure a pool mathematically.
questions.explain: 第2句 "it was already too late to avert a flood of her own making"——avert（a 离开 + vert 转）指把事情转开、防止它发生；她已来不及阻止这场自己哭出来的洪水。

sentences.en: "What is a Caucus-race?" asked Alice, and the dodo answered that the best way to explain it was to do it, for talking, in its long experience, never informed anybody of anything that could be learned by running; and as the party was wet, and the afternoon long, nobody contradicted this proposition.
sentences.zh: "什么是会议式赛跑？"爱丽丝问。渡渡鸟回答：最好的解释办法就是跑一遍——依它多年的经验，凡是跑步能学会的事，光靠说是从来教不会任何人的；大家又湿着，午后又长，于是没有人反驳这个提议。

sentences.en: The dodo marked out a course in a rough circle — the exact shape, it said, not mattering — and there was no starting and no finishing post, and the party was placed here and there, and ran when it liked and stopped when it liked, all of which was understood by everybody except the one runner who won, there being no such runner.
sentences.zh: 渡渡鸟圈出一条大致圆形的跑道——它说，形状准不准无所谓；没有起点，也没有终点；大家东一个西一个站好，想跑就跑，想停就停——这一切人人都懂，唯独那个跑赢了的例外；因为压根没有这么一位。

sentences.en: They ran for half an hour or so, by the end of which everybody was quite dry, and the dodo called out, "The race is over!" — and every bird and beast sat down at once, panting, and asked who had won, a question the dodo had been preparing itself to receive for the full half hour, the whole half hour having been one long rehearsal.
sentences.zh: 他们跑了半个小时左右，跑到最后人人都干了；渡渡鸟喊道："赛跑结束！"——于是飞禽走兽一齐坐下来喘气，齐声问：谁赢了？这个问题，渡渡鸟整半小时都在备着答案，专等人来问——那整整半小时，本来就是一场漫长的排练。

sentences.en: "But who has won?" asked Alice, who had a plain mind and expected a plain answer; the dodo thought long, with its eyes closed, and then said that everybody had won, and all must have prizes — a verdict which nobody contradicted, chiefly because nobody could tell what it would mean.
sentences.zh: "可到底谁赢了呢？"爱丽丝问——她是个直心眼，盼着一句直话；渡渡鸟闭上眼睛想了很久很久，然后宣布：人人都赢了，人人都要有奖品。这个裁决没有人反驳，主要是因为谁也说不清它究竟是什么意思。

sentences.en: "Who is to give the prizes?" was the next question, and it was decided at once that Alice must, and she had a box of sweets in her pocket, just enough to go round, though by what formula each flavour found its runner, not even the dodo could say.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题是："奖品由谁来发？"大家当场议定：非爱丽丝莫属。她口袋里正好有一盒糖果，分一圈不多不少；至于按什么章法让每种口味找到自己的主人，连渡渡鸟也说不清。

sentences.en: The sweets were handed round and eaten, some before the ceremony was over, and then, finding herself the only one without a prize, Alice received her own thimble back from the dodo with great formality, and as solemnly as she could manage, while the animals cheered — the thimble being, by weight, the least prize and, by ceremony, the greatest.
sentences.zh: 糖果挨个分下去，有些没等仪式结束就进了肚；随后大家发现只剩爱丽丝一人没有奖品，渡渡鸟便郑重其事地把她自己先前交出去的顶针颁还给她；她竭尽全力庄严地收下，动物们一片欢呼——这枚顶针，论分量是全场最轻的奖品，论仪式，却是分量最重的一枚。

sentences.en: The Mouse then offered to tell its long history — the history that had once been a tale and once a tail — but one by one the animals drifted away, like notes leaving a page of music, and no story was begun, and no story, in that company, ever would be.
sentences.zh: 老鼠接着提议讲它长长的经历——就是那桩一会儿是"故事"、一会儿是"尾巴"的经历——可动物们一个个散了，像音符从乐谱上飘走；故事终究没有开场，而且在这群听众中间，永远也开不了场。

sentences.en: Alice stayed to listen, first out of politeness and then out of a real sadness; but the Mouse's voice came from farther and farther off, as if told from the bottom of the pool, which by now was only a memory of water, warm and salt and going nowhere.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝留下来想听，先是出于礼貌，后来是当真难过；可老鼠的声音越来越远，像是从池底讲出来的——而那池子，到这时也只剩一段关于水的回忆了：温的，咸的，哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: The hall grew dim, and the crowd of creatures faded like wet paper held up to the light, their colours running together, until only their voices remained, and then not even those; and Alice, alone in the dimness, understood that something enormous and gentle was closing over the whole afternoon.
sentences.zh: 大厅暗了下来，那群动物像对着光举起的湿纸一样褪去，颜色一层层洇开，先是只剩下声音，最后连声音也没有了；爱丽丝独自站在昏暗里，明白有什么巨大而温柔的东西，正轻轻合拢，罩住这一整个下午。

sentences.en: "You are only a dream," she told them, or perhaps told herself, "and maybe I am somebody's dream too; who can predict where a dream begins, or whose sleeping head it is walking about in?" — and this thought, which should have frightened her, struck her instead as a great and curious mercy.
sentences.zh: "你们只是一场梦，"她对它们说，也许是对自己说，"说不定我也是别人梦里的东西；谁能预言一场梦从哪儿开头，又走在谁的睡着的脑袋里呢？"——这个念头本该吓着她，落在她心上，反倒成了一种巨大而奇妙的慈悲。

sentences.en: In one last transformation, the water became grass, the grass became a river bank, the bank held her sister, reading on exactly as before, and the warm afternoon, with all its creatures folded inside it, was handed back to Alice as a single sentence: "I have had such a curious dream."
sentences.zh: 在最后一次变化里，池水变成了草地，草地变成了河岸，河岸上坐着她的姐姐，正同从前一样读着书；那个暖洋洋的下午，连同叠在里面的所有动物，被一并交还给爱丽丝，收成一句话："我做了一个好奇怪的梦。"

sentences.en: She described the metamorphosis, the tears, and the race that everybody won, and her sister, who could see none of it, listened kindly, and smoothed her hair, and said that she would wake tomorrow and remember it — which was true — and that it would all be gone — which was not entirely so.
sentences.zh: 她讲了自己的变形、那些眼泪，还有那场人人都赢的赛跑；姐姐什么也看不见，却和气地听着，抚着她的头发，说：明天一早醒来，你还会记得它——这半句是真的；又说：到时候这一切就都不见了——这半句，倒不见得。

sentences.en: But her sister, sitting on in the warm dusk, kept her eyes on the river, and half believed, for a minute, that she heard the tiny clatter of the Caucus-race far off, and the faint treble of a rabbit asking the time — that other universe, with its formalities and its verdicts, lying very near to this one, and only one sleep away.
sentences.zh: 可她的姐姐在暖融融的暮色里坐下去，眼睛望着河面，有一分钟竟半信半疑：她听见远处传来会议式赛跑细细的哒哒声，还有一只兔子尖细的嗓音在报时——那个另外的宇宙，连同它的一套礼数和裁决，就躺在这一个的近旁，中间只隔一场睡眠。

sentences.en: For a sister who has been told the whole of a dream will dream the edges of it herself; and the grass rustled, and the pool — that there was no pool — and the bank was quiet, and the book, patient to the last, waited without pictures and without conversations for somebody to begin it again.
sentences.zh: 因为一个听完了整个梦的姐姐，自己也会梦到梦的边角；草在沙沙响，池水——本没有池水——岸上安安静静；那本书耐心到了极点，依旧没有插图、没有对话，等着有谁再来翻开第一页。

questions.q: How did the dodo explain what a Caucus-race was?
options: By drawing the course on paper.
By making everybody simply run it, since talking never informed anybody.
By reciting a long list of rules.
By dictating a formal speech about running.
questions.explain: 第1句渡渡鸟说 "the best way to explain it was to do it, for talking... never informed anybody of anything that could be learned by running"——最好的解释就是跑一遍。

questions.q: What was the verdict of the Caucus-race?
options: The dodo alone had won.
Nobody had really won at all.
Everybody had won, and all must have prizes.
The race would have to be run again.
questions.explain: 第4句 "everybody had won, and all must have prizes — a verdict which nobody contradicted"，人人有奖的裁决无人反驳——因为谁也说不清它什么意思。

questions.q: What prize did Alice herself receive?
options: A sweet from her own pocket.
A medal made by the dodo.
Nothing at all, like the Mouse.
Her own thimble, handed back with great formality.
questions.explain: 第6句 "finding herself the only one without a prize, Alice received her own thimble back from the dodo with great formality"——她把自己交出去的顶针，被郑重其事地颁还给了她。

questions.q: At the end, the sister keeps her eyes on the river and half believes she hears the race. What does this suggest?
options: That she is planning to follow the rabbit herself tomorrow.
That the dream world lies very close to the ordinary one, separated only by a sleep.
That Alice has not really woken up yet.
That the sister will write the story down for a book.
questions.explain: 第13句她"半信半疑"地听见了赛跑声和兔子报时，说那个另外的宇宙"lying very near to this one, and only one sleep away"——可知在卡罗尔笔下，那个奇幻世界离平常的世界只隔一场睡眠。

questions.q: With dict meaning to say, what is a "verdict" in sentence 4?
options: A kind of race run in a circle.
A formal statement or decision that something is so — here, the dodo's ruling that all had won.
A box of sweets shared among runners.
A prize given to the fastest animal.
questions.explain: 第4句 "a verdict which nobody contradicted, chiefly because nobody could tell what it would mean"——verdict（ver 真实 + dict 说）指郑重宣布的决定、裁决，即渡渡鸟"人人皆赢、人人有奖"的裁定。
